downside.story: P10: AI demand digests in 2027. Anthropic and OpenAI, a large share of the $578B backlog, slow their commitments, so AWS FY2027 growth falls to ~23% and the margin drops 3 points as the D&A from $300B+ of capex lands on lower utilization. Retail margin stalls (Leo ramp, FTC remedies on ads). The P/E de-rates to ~19x on ~$9.7 NTM EPS, and the Anthropic stake is marked down 40%.

base.story: Median: AWS converts the $578B backlog as capacity lands (+39.5% in 2027, +33% in 2028) at ~37.5% margins despite the D&A wave. Ads grow mid-to-high teens and the retail margin creeps up ~0.7 points a year. EPS reaches ~$12.3 in 2028, ~12% under consensus, and the market pays ~24x NTM core EPS plus the stakes.

upside.story: P90: capacity converts the backlog faster. AWS grows ~50% in 2027 (above UBS's 43%) at ~40% margins as Trainium lowers cost per token, ads hold ~20% growth, and the market pays ~27x NTM EPS of ~$14. An Anthropic IPO re-marks the stake 40% higher.

reasoning: Rerun on current data (the earlier file used Oct 5-6 consensus and predated the Q3 print). Primary lane: the Q3 2026 release and 10-Q, the Q4 2025, Q1 and Q2 2026 releases (segment and ad tables, quarterly guides), XBRL quarterly capex/D&A/interest, and call excerpts with speakers. Key facts: Q3 revenue $201.9B (+12%), AWS $46.0B (+39%, 38.7% margin), ads $19.6B (+11%), operating income $28.1B (a record 13.9% margin). Q4 guide: $240-247B revenue and $28.5-33.5B operating income, ads 'high teens'. AWS backlog $578B (6.1-year life, +$82B q/q). TTM FCF -$42.4B on $215B TTM capex. 2026 capex ~$220B, 'meaningfully more' in 2027 (CEO). Anthropic carried at $238.7B and OpenAI at $35B in the 10-Q. Model: AWS grows +39.5% in FY2027 and +33% in FY2028 (sequential adds capped by capacity; 3.5 points under UBS's 43%) at a 37.5% margin, below 2026 as D&A climbs. Ads grow +17%/+15%, retail ex-ads +8.5%/+8%, and the retail margin rises +0.7/+0.6 points on the ads mix. Capex follows the project's Big-4 path at Amazon's 2026 share ($303.5B and $392.5B). The result: FY2027 revenue $962B (consensus $960B), EBIT $147B (consensus $147B), and FY2028 EBIT $187B (5% under consensus) with EPS $12.33 vs $14.58. Valuation: P/E with the 0.8 shrink, and a SOTP; stakes added after tax and illiquidity. Research target (12m) $322.8 (+24%). It sits close to the sell-side mean ($326.5) for a different reason: below-consensus EPS on a higher multiple of core earnings once the $18/share of stakes is taken out of today's multiple. Scenarios: P10 $209 (AWS -12% revenue and -3pt margin, multiple -5 turns, SOTP multiples -20%, stakes -40%) and P90 $419 (AWS +10% revenue and +2.5pt margin, multiple +3, SOTP multiples +12%, stakes +40%). The left tail is fatter, matching the AI capex digestion risk and the stock's 34% realized volatility. Decart: reported near a ~$7-7.5B deal but not signed; left out as value-neutral.

drivers.label: AWS net sales
drivers.source: Actual quarters: segment tables in the Q4 2025, Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 releases. Forecast: AWS backlog $578B (10-Q, CEO Jassy), Q3 run rate $184B, capacity from the capex path.
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY2026 $49.7B (+39.7% y/y; sequential +$3.7B, the same add as Q3's +$3.75B, because AWS is capacity-limited and Q4 capacity lands mainly in the back half). FY2027: quarterly adds of $4.2B, 4.6, 5.0 and 5.4B as the 2026-27 capex ($226B and $303.5B, see capex row) comes online -> $244.8B (+39.5%). FY2028: adds of $5.0B a quarter -> $325.6B (+33.0%). Cross-checks: the backlog of $578B over a 6.1-year weighted life is ~$95B a year of contracted revenue on top of the on-demand base. It rose $82B in Q3 alone (from $496B in Q2). UBS (Nov 18) has 2027 AWS +43%. We sit 3.5 points below UBS (moderately conservative base, rule 0c): power and chip delivery have capped sequential adds at $3.7-4.6B a quarter in 2026. Alternatives: (a) UBS +43% 2027 growth -> FY2027 ~$251B (+2.5%); (b) backlog burn only (~$95B/yr contracted plus a flat on-demand base) -> ~+30% (-$15B FY2027).
drivers.why: AWS revenue is the line the AI capex is spent on. Backlog and capacity, not the disclosed segment, set its path; it is kept as one driver because Amazon does not disclose GW or GPU counts that would allow a units x price build.
drivers.quarter_derivation: actual quarters from the releases; forecast quarters as in derivation

drivers.label: AWS operating margin
drivers.source: Actual quarters: AWS operating income / AWS net sales from the releases. Forecast: depreciation path (da row) and the CEO's comments on depreciation.
drivers.derivation: Q1-Q3 2026: 37.7%, 39.4%, 38.7%. Q4 FY2026 38.0%: Q3 less ~0.7 points for the ~$1.05B sequential D&A step (da row), mostly AWS servers. FY2027-28 37.5%: consolidated D&A rises from 10.0% of revenue (FY2026) to 11.6% (FY2027) and 13.3% (FY2028), and ~80% of the step is AWS. Scale on a fixed cost base and backlog pricing offset it, so the margin holds 1 point below the 2026 average. UBS cut its 2027 AWS margin to 40% from 45% (Nov 18). We sit 2.5 points below UBS because our capex path is above the $298.7B consensus. Alternatives: UBS 40% -> +$6.1B FY2027 EBIT; FY2025 average 35.4% -> -$5.1B.
drivers.why: The D&A wave from AI capex against AWS pricing power is the main earnings debate.
drivers.quarter_derivation: actual quarters from the releases; forecast quarters as in derivation

drivers.label: Advertising services revenue
drivers.source: Actual quarters: net sales by group in the Q4 2025, Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 releases. Q4 FY2026 guide: "high teens" y/y (Q3 release).
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY2026 $24.94B = Q4 FY2025 $21.317B x 1.17. That is the low end of "high teens" because Q3 grew only 12% ex-FX (Prime Day and other timing per the release) and the FTC ad-auction suit pressures pricing (src FTC). FY2027 +17% on the same quarter of FY2026 (Prime Video ads full year, DSP; the exit rate from the Q4 guide) and FY2028 +15% (law of large numbers; the FY2025-26 pace was +23% then +19%). Quarter shape = the FY2026 quarters. Variant: +20%/yr adds ~$3B FY2028 EBIT at ~50% incremental margin.
drivers.why: Ads carry most of the retail segment's margin gain, so ads mix is a separate driver.
drivers.quarter_derivation: actual quarters from the releases; forecast quarters as in derivation
drivers.variant_view: +20%/yr adds ~$3B FY2028 EBIT at ~50% incremental margin.

drivers.label: Retail ex-ads revenue (online/physical stores, 3P seller services, subscriptions, other)
drivers.source: Actual quarters: North America + International segment sales less advertising (releases).
drivers.derivation: Q4 FY2026 = Q4 FY2025 $156.49B x 1.095. The FY2026 run-rate: Q2+Q3 combined +9.7% y/y, which nets out the Prime Day shift between Q2 and Q3; Q1 +12.6%. The Q4 FX assumption is -60bp (Q3 release). FY2027 +8.5%, FY2028 +8.0%: unit growth slows as 2026 FX tailwinds fade, and 3P services and subscriptions grow with units. Consolidated Q4 revenue then comes to $246.0B, inside the $240-247B guide. Variant: +10%/yr (2026 pace held) -> +$9B FY2027 revenue, ~+$0.7B EBIT.
drivers.why: Units x price in the stores business are not disclosed. Retail ex-ads is the volume line the retail margin applies to.
drivers.quarter_derivation: actual quarters from the releases; forecast quarters as in derivation

drivers.label: North America + International operating margin (on ads + stores revenue)

FY2028 +0.6 points. Alternative: the FY2025->26 step of +1.15 points held -> +$3.3B FY2027 EBIT.

FY2027-28 = Amazon's 2026 share of Big-4 capex (225.7/750.7 = 30.07%) x the project's Big-4 path ($1,009.45B, $1,305.26B) = $303.5B and $392.5B, rising through each year.

downside.story: P10: AI demand digests in 2027. Anthropic and OpenAI, a large share of the $578B backlog, slow their commitments, so AWS FY2027 growth falls to ~23% and the margin drops 3 points as the D&A from $300B+ of capex lands on lower utilization. Retail margin stalls (Leo ramp, FTC remedies on ads). The P/E de-rates to ~19x on ~$9.7 NTM EPS, and the Anthropic stake is marked down 40%.

upside.story: P90: capacity converts the backlog faster. AWS grows ~50% in 2027 (above UBS's 43%) at ~40% margins as Trainium lowers cost per token, ads hold ~20% growth, and the market pays ~27x NTM EPS of ~$14. An Anthropic IPO re-marks the stake 40% higher.

inputs_detail.derivation: Q4 FY2026 $49.7B (+39.7% y/y; sequential +$3.7B, the same add as Q3's +$3.75B, because AWS is capacity-limited and Q4 capacity lands mainly in the back half). FY2027: quarterly adds of $4.2B, 4.6, 5.0 and 5.4B as the 2026-27 capex ($226B and $303.5B, see capex row) comes online -> $244.8B (+39.5%). FY2028: adds of $5.0B a quarter -> $325.6B (+33.0%). Cross-checks: the backlog of $578B over a 6.1-year weighted life is ~$95B a year of contracted revenue on top of the on-demand base. It rose $82B in Q3 alone (from $496B in Q2). UBS (Nov 18) has 2027 AWS +43%. We sit 3.5 points below UBS (moderately conservative base, rule 0c): power and chip delivery have capped sequential adds at $3.7-4.6B a quarter in 2026. Alternatives: (a) UBS +43% 2027 growth -> FY2027 ~$251B (+2.5%); (b) backlog burn only (~$95B/yr contracted plus a flat on-demand base) -> ~+30% (-$15B FY2027).

Q1-Q3 2026: 37.7%, 39.4%, 38.7%. Q4 FY2026 38.0%: Q3 less ~0.7 points for the ~$1.05B sequential D&A step (da row), mostly AWS servers. FY2027-28 37.5%: consolidated D&A rises from 10.0% of revenue (FY2026) to 11.6% (FY2027) and 13.3% (FY2028), and ~80% of the step is AWS. Scale on a fixed cost base and backlog pricing offset it, so the margin holds 1 point below the 2026 average. UBS cut its 2027 AWS margin to 40% from 45% (Nov 18). We sit 2.5 points below UBS because our capex path is above the $298.7B consensus. Alternatives: UBS 40% -> +$6.1B FY2027 EBIT; FY2025 average 35.4% -> -$5.1B.

track_record.note: Only one full year with a first guide (Q4-24 run rate ~$105B). FY2026's first guide was ~$200B (Feb 5), raised to ~$220B (Jul 30) and reiterated Oct 29. The record is of overspending the first guide.

guidance_check.why: The record-adjusted ~$276B is not credible for one quarter: it would need Q4 at ~$100B against $77B in Q3. Instead the Q4 row is set at $50B, the Q1-Q2 2026 average pace ($49.2B), because the CEO reiterated ~$220B on Oct 29 knowing Q3's $77B. We sit $5.7B above the guide (gross vs net of incentives, and the overspend record). guide_use: kind 'guide_plus'. why_nothing_better: no Q4 capex plan, shipment schedule or data-center delivery count is disclosed, and Q4 capex cannot be built bottom-up from public data. The Q3 run-rate ($77B, FY $253B) contradicts the company's statement made after seeing Q3; the record ratio gives an implausible Q4. Tried builds: Q3 run-rate (rejected, contradicts the reiterated guide); record x guide (rejected, implausible Q4).

guide_use.why_nothing_better: No Q4 capex plan, chip-shipment schedule or data-center delivery count is disclosed. The only forward evidence is the CEO's reiterated ~$220B, made on Oct 29 after Q3's $77.3B. A Q3 run-rate would put FY2026 at ~$253B against that statement; a record ratio would need a ~$100B Q4.

comps_summary.our_multiple_vs_peers: Own NTM P/E ex stakes 22.6x = ($259.33 - $18.0 per share of Anthropic/OpenAI stakes after tax and liquidity discount) / FY2027 consensus EPS $10.66 (MarketScreener, 2026-11-20). That is a 31% discount to the 32.8x median. Exit P/E = 32.8 x (22.6/32.8)^0.8 = 24.4x on our own GAAP NTM EPS (~$12.1 at the horizon), ~26% below the median and inside the peer range.
comps_summary.premium_discount_justification: No premium is argued. The k = 0.8 shrink keeps ~80% of today's discount, which has persisted: capex at ~30-35% of revenue in 2027-28 makes levered FCF negative (consensus FCF -$24.3B in 2027), and a ~71% retail mix earns lower margins than WMT/COST multiples imply. The SOTP leg uses 20x / 21x EV/EBIT: AWS at MSFT-level after-tax earnings multiples because it grows ~2x faster with a $578B backlog, and retail at a discount to retail peers for margin and the Leo drag.
comps_summary.peer_count_flag: 8 whole-company peers (+META segment-only). No more genuine comparables: the other large e-commerce/cloud platforms (Alibaba, JD, PDD, Coupang, NAVER) are excluded by the China/Korea structural-discount rule; eBay and Etsy are low-growth marketplaces with no cloud and are not in the run's table. Fewer is better than padding.

model_inputs.structure_note: Quarterly driver-led set (16 quarters, 7 reported). Two segments built from 5 drivers: AWS = aws_rev x aws_m; North America + International = (ads_rev + stores_rev) x retail_m. D&A, capex, interest expense and interest income are cited quarter constants. The value is carried by (1) a P/E leg (60%) at 24.4x on the model's own NTM GAAP EPS (after SBC and interest, ex equity marks) and (2) a SOTP leg (40%) with AWS at 20x and retail at 21x NTM EV/EBIT; both are driver-linked through the quarter rows. Anthropic ($238.7B carried) and OpenAI ($35B) sit in stakes after tax and liquidity haircuts on every leg, plus a probability-weighted FTC adjustment. No DCF leg (Consumer Discretionary, not a neocloud); no FCF-yield leg (AMZN is not in the tech FCF-leg list, and levered FCF is negative). Leg weights are judgment, untested. Driver set: these ids mirror the approved AMZN set's segment logic (AWS / retail with ads separated) but AWS is driven by revenue and operating margin instead of PP&E x turnover x EBITDA margin, because quarterly AWS PP&E was not retrievable here (SEC fetches of the segment note truncated). Flag for Kilian: a driver change vs the approved set.
model_inputs.gap_note: For Kilian: (1) Driver ids differ from the approved AMZN set (aws_ppe/aws_turn/aws_ebitda_m replaced by aws_rev/aws_m), see structure_note; needs a card before it is booked. (2) FY2026 Q4 capex sits on the ~$220B guide plus a gross/net gap (guide_use declared in guidance_check). (3) Base-year quarter splits of interest expense/income (FY2025 spread evenly) and the Q2 2025 capex are derived; they do not enter the valuation. (4) Quarter shapes for ads/stores FY2027-28 use the FY2026 quarters, i.e. one year's shape (2026 had the Prime Day shift into Q2). Fewer than 3 years of the ads quarter split were retrieved; flagged under rule 9. (5) Decart (~$7-7.5B, not signed) is left out as value-neutral, below 20% materiality. (6) Judgment calls sized: cloud-only AWS multiple (~-8%) and the k=1 alternative (~-4%); the AWS EV/EBIT basis exceeds 5% and goes to a card. (7) fair_value.value equals the engine's base horizon value.
